have hh' := congrArg (Ideal.map (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of R)).hom.hom) hh
  have he : (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of R)).hom.hom.comp
      (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of R)).inv.hom = RingHom.id R := by
    exact congrArg CommRingCat.Hom.hom (Iso.inv_hom_id (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of R)))
  simpa only [Ideal.map_map, he, Ideal.map_id] using hh'
findings.problem: After extracting the ideals on the top affine open, the proof maps them back and manually proves that the two ring homomorphisms compose to the identity. That category-level detour obscures the simple point: the top-open ideals are related by a ring equivalence, so mapping back along its inverse recovers the original ideals.
findings.proposed_change:
Replace the proof body with:
```lean
  intro I J h
  have hh := congrArg (fun A => A.ideal ⟨⊤, isAffineOpen_top (Spec (.of R))⟩) h
  let e : R ≃+* Γ(Spec (.of R), ⊤) :=
    (Scheme.ΓSpecIso (.of R)).symm.commRingCatIsoToRingEquiv
  have hh' := congrArg (Ideal.map (e.symm : Γ(Spec (.of R), ⊤) →+* R)) hh
  simpa only [specIdeal_top, Ideal.map_of_equiv] using hh'
```
findings.benefit: This keeps the same top-open argument while replacing the manually derived composition identity with `Ideal.map_of_equiv`. The named equivalence makes it at least as easy to follow why mapping back recovers the original ideals, and removes the intermediate category-hom calculation.

theorem map_of_equiv {I : Ideal R} (f : R ≃+* S) :
    (I.map (f : R →+* S)).map (f.symm : S →+* R) = I := by
